name: table

capacity.note: the table density crowds past six rows

handles.note: The projection reads a row as `<label>: <cell>; <cell>.`, which no single element on the slide holds — so the cue hid. The row's first cell is the label it opens with.

split.note: In a PORTRAIT box a wide read-across table can't paginate out of HORIZONTAL overflow, so it RESHAPES: each row becomes a card (column headers -> in-card labels), then the cards cover-paginate (accent cover -> card pages). ONE card per page: a transposed row is a card (a header plus its labeled fields), and a card is one page's worth -- the same heavy-member rule capacity.perPage:1 applies on the plain-axis path (cards-grid, cards-stack, actors, policy-recommendation). Landscape renders the native table. lib/core/carousel.js cover-cards; engineering/decisions/2026-06-25-retire-landscape-locks-portrait-everything.md.

description: The table component — a GFM pipe table with a row capacity, autosplit, and the portrait card reshape.
purpose: Use when the table IS the slide. A plain markdown table on any slide already gets the house treatment; reach for this when the rows need a capacity budget, autosplit, focus axes, or the portrait reshape.

title.description: Slide heading framing what the table shows.

table.description: Markdown table with a header row and 2+ data rows. Column alignment is markdown's own (`:---`, `:---:`, `---:`).

whenToUse.title: The table IS the slide
whenToUse.body: A plain markdown table on any slide already gets the house treatment — same type, rails, hairlines and zebra. Reach for `table` when the rows need what only a component can declare: a capacity budget, autosplit, the portrait card reshape, and the `row`/`col`/`cell` focus axes.

whenToUse.title: Three or more columns, or four or more rows
whenToUse.body: `compare-prose` maxes out at two options with prose bodies. A table scales past that, as long as the cells stay short.

whenToUse.title: Cells are short phrases
whenToUse.body: Each cell is a value, a phrase, or a state marker — not a paragraph. If the cells need sentences, use `verdict-grid` or `cards-stack`.

whenToUse.title: Stable column meaning
whenToUse.body: Every row reads the same way across columns. Mixing column meanings row-to-row breaks the table's scannability.

antiPatterns.title: Cells full of prose
antiPatterns.body: Long sentences in a cell wrap awkwardly and force the column wider. Move to `verdict-grid` for criteria with body text, or `cards-stack` for full prose rows.

antiPatterns.title: More than 6 rows
antiPatterns.body: Past 6 rows the table crowds the slide. Split across two slides or summarize the rows that don't differentiate.

antiPatterns.title: A table that only supports the prose around it
antiPatterns.body: Then it does not need this class at all — write the pipe table on a `content` or un-classed slide and the universal treatment styles it. The component is for a table that owns the slide.

antiPatterns.title: Reaching for it when a specialist fits better
antiPatterns.body: Mostly pass/fail badges is `obligation-matrix` or `verdict-grid`; term/definition pairs are `glossary`; a dated plan is `roadmap`.

related.name: compare-prose
related.when: exactly two options with prose bodies

related.name: verdict-grid

related.name: obligation-matrix
related.when: many regimes compared against shared obligations

related.name: cards-stack

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing a vague or duplicate first column, assuming it's just another data column.
commonMistakes.fix: When the table overflows a narrow box, the Fit Ladder reshapes it into row-cards (column headers become in-card labels) instead of clipping — the FIRST column becomes each card's title in that reshape, so it needs to be a genuinely identifying label per row. This happens automatically and needs no opt-in.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting the first column's `**bold**` to show when the column is already emphasized as a row label.
commonMistakes.fix: The row-label emphasis sets the same weight and ink `**bold**` would, so bolding inside it is a no-op. `no-row-label` turns the emphasis off and hands the column back to you.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reaching for a CSS override to make a short table fill the slide.
commonMistakes.fix: `table-fill` is the switch — it grows the table AND centers each cell in its band. The default hugs the rows and centers the block, so a three-row table reads as three rows rather than three rows stretched over a screen.
